findings.passage: The Senate has always been committed to having the strongest gun safety laws in the nation, and we remain firm in our resolve to pass a comprehensive gun safety and violence prevention bill this session.
findings.note: Statement issued in her name after the Lewiston shooting; the page is dated 2023-10-26. She commits the Senate to a comprehensive gun safety bill.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: By bringing together stakeholders with a variety of viewpoints, the Senate has shown that it is possible to make changes to our gun laws that will save lives while respecting the rights of law-abiding gun owners in the state.
findings.note: Quote in her official press release when the Senate unveiled the SAFER Act (page published 2024-01-25).

findings.passage: I’m proud to lead a body that is committed to building on our Commonwealth’s record as a national leader on gun safety.
findings.note: Quote in her official press release after the Senate passed the SAFER Act (page published 2024-02-01).

findings.passage: "Our state, I think all of you know, has one of the lowest rates of gun violence in the nation, and this fact is not by accident," Senate President Karen Spilka said.
findings.note: Quoted by NBC Boston (article published 2024-01-27) at the unveiling of the Senate gun bill; says the state has updated its gun laws to prevent access by people who wish to do harm.
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: "The vast majority of Massachusetts residents wants this bill and want it to take effect as soon as possible," said Massachusetts Senate President Karen Spilka.
findings.note: Quoted by NBC Boston (article published 2024-10-02) on the 2024 gun law and the effort to suspend it.
